name: Hairy chest transplant / body hair transplant

card.summary: Surgical transfer of follicles by FUE; published work concerns moving body hair to the scalp, and cosmetic chest-hair transplants are barely studied.
card.aka: BHT, FUE to body, chest hair transplant
card.note: Most published body-hair transplant research is about using body hair as a donor for the scalp, not adding chest hair.

quick.overview:
Body hair transplant moves individual follicles by follicular unit extraction (FUE) from one area to another. In the literature the usual direction is body-to-scalp, for men who lack scalp donor hair. Looksmaxxing posts about a 'hairy chest transplant' apply FUE to the chest itself.

Surgeons have published case series and small studies of body hair as scalp donor hair, and uses in scars and vitiligo. No studies of transplanting hair onto the chest for appearance were found in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: Follicular units of one to four hairs are extracted with small punches and implanted individually. Transplanted hair is described as retaining the growth characteristics of its donor area. Body hair has a high share of follicles in resting phase, which one study addressed by shaving donor sites days before extraction.
quick.risks: Reported issues include temporary shedding of transplanted hair (anagen effluvium), variable graft survival, and the general risks of surgery. Reference sources say body hair differs from scalp hair in texture and growth rate. Cost varies widely by country.

lead: Body hair transplantation (BHT) is a form of follicular unit extraction (FUE) in which follicles are harvested from body regions such as the beard, chest or limbs [1][2]. The published literature mostly concerns using body hair as additional donor supply for balding scalps, and uses in scars, cicatricial alopecia and vitiligo [1][3][5][6].

Looksmaxxing discussions of a 'hairy chest transplant' propose using the technique to add hair to a sparse chest. No published study of that cosmetic use was found; the evidence consists of body-to-scalp series and case reports. A 122-patient series reported outcomes of body hair transplanted to the scalp [1].

paras: FUE removes follicular units individually with small punches and places them in recipient sites, avoiding the linear scar of strip harvesting; it is described as time-consuming and technique-dependent [2]. Reference sources say BHT can only be done by FUE and requires an experienced surgeon, and that texture and growth-rate differences between body and scalp hair should be considered [11].
Many body hairs are in the resting (telogen) phase and occur as single-hair units. One group proposed shaving donor body hair four days before extraction to identify anagen hairs [4].

A series of 122 patients with adequate body hair who received body hair transplanted to bald scalp areas between 2005 and 2011 was published in 2016 [1]; an accompanying commentary also appeared [8]. A comparative study examined rates of anagen effluvium and survival of scalp, beard and chest hair in scalp hair restoration [7]. Other reports cover body hair transplant for cicatricial alopecia [3], vitiligo [5] and a wide donor scar [6]. A registered vitiligo hair-transplant trial was withdrawn [9], and a trial of a protocol to improve follicle survival in FUE is registered and not yet recruiting [10]. No studies of transplanting hair to the chest for cosmetic purposes were found.

Reference sources list temporary shedding ('shock loss'), reduced graft survival with smoking or alcohol, infection requiring antibiotics in some cases, and some surgeons' reports of lower graft success for FUE than strip surgery [11]. Costs per graft are reported to range from about US$1 in Turkey to US$7 in Canada [11].

timeline.event: Period of the 122-patient body hair FUE series [1].
Series and commentary published in Aesthetic Surgery Journal [1][8].
